title: Quomodo Trinitas Unus Deus Ac Non Tres Dii
author: Boethius

passages.original: præteralteritatem enim nec pluralitas quid sit intelligi potest.Trium namquererum vel quotlibet tum genere tum specie,tum numero diversitas constat: quoties enim idem dicitur, toties diversum etiam praedicatur. Idem vero dicitur tribus modis:aut genere,utidem homo quod equus, quia his idem genus,ut animal; vel specie, ut idem Cato quod Cicero. quia eadem species ut humo ; vel numero, ut Tullius et Cicero quia unus est numero. Quare diversum etiam vel genere, vel specie, vel numero dicitur; sed numero differentiam accidentium varietas facit: nam tres homines neque genere, neque specie, sed suis accidentibus distant.
passages.english: For apart from otherness it cannot even be understood what plurality is. For the difference of three things, or of any number, consists in genus, or in species, or in number: for as often as "the same" is said, so often is "different" also predicated. Now "the same" is said in three ways: either in genus, as a man is the same as a horse, because they have the same genus, namely animal; or in species, as Cato is the same as Cicero, because [they have] the same species, namely man; or in number, as Tully and Cicero, because [he] is one in number. Therefore "different" is also said either in genus, or in species, or in number; but difference in number is produced by variety of accidents: for three men differ neither in genus nor in species, but by their accidents.
